Hi Anna / Acme procurement team,

Hope you’re doing well. Our records show your annual term is up for renewal on 2027-01-31 and you flagged earlier this quarter that usage is trending 35% above the committed baseline. I’d like to kick off a short renewal + expansion coordination so we can:

- Confirm updated committed capacity and any planned uplift for H1 2027
- Walk through proposed term adjustments (pricing tiers and any SLA addenda)
- Schedule a QBR to review usage, cost optimizations (batching/quantization recommendations), and roadmap alignment

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick sync (30 min) to confirm capacity delta and target term length — are you available Weds 12/2 or Thurs 12/3, late morning PT?
2) I’ll circulate a short renewal playbook and proposed SLA addendum for your review (attached)
3) QBR tentatively the week of 12/14 — we can lock a concrete slot after the sync

If procurement prefers, we can also handle pricing details by email and have legal review the SLA addendum in parallel.

Attaching: redwood-renewal-playbook.pdf (overview), proposed-sla-addendum.docx (draft)

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

Best,
Priyom Das

Thanks for confirming, Anna — 12/2 11:00 AM PT is locked on our calendars.

To answer your questions ahead of the call:
1) SLA addendum: The draft attached raises the uptime credit band for committed capacity thresholds to 99.9% for mission-critical routes and includes a step-down credit schedule if we fail SLOs tied to the expanded capacity. We can walk through exact credit math in the call.
2) Rollback plan: We recommend a three-month staged uplift with monthly checkpoints. If usage drops >25% vs the uplift baseline within a month, we propose a 30-day cooling period and an option to reduce committed capacity at the next monthly checkpoint without penalty. We’ll outline contract language for that during negotiations.

For the pricing ask: Pricing for incremental committed units is tiered — I’ll pull the proposed numbers into a short spreadsheet and have it in the HubSpot deal before EOD. (Link to draft will be posted to the HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.redwood.net/deals/ACME-4598)

Agenda for 12/2 (30 min):
- 5 min: recapped usage and proposed uplift
- 10 min: term options (12 vs 24 months) and pricing for uplift bands
- 10 min: SLA addendum highlights and rollback provisions
- 5 min: agreed next steps and decisioning timeline

I’ve attached the playbook and SLA again for reference. Priyom — can you please bring the signed PO template and the draft MSA redline tracker? Karthik — would you be able to join for the pricing/technical implications?

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Account Strategy | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0210

Great conversation yesterday — thanks everyone for the time. Quick recap and next steps below.

Recap:
- Agreed uplift target: +35% committed units starting 2027-01-01, with a staged review cadence (monthly checkpoints in Jan/Feb/Mar).
- Term length: Acme prefers a 12-month renewal with an option to extend at the same rates for an additional 12 months.
- SLA: We’ll finalize the addendum with the 99.9% credit band for mission routes and include the rollback clause with a 30-day cooling period.

Action items / owners:
- Redwood (Lauren) — post updated pricing spreadsheet to HubSpot (link: https://hubspot.redwood.net/deals/ACME-4598) and file the draft SOW for procurement review by 12/7.
- Redwood (Karthik) — provide technical notes on burst capacity and recommended batching settings for the new feature by 12/9.
- Acme (Procurement) — review draft SLA and SOW; aim to provide redline by 12/14.
- Both — schedule QBR for the week of 12/14. Priyom to send calendar options.

I’ve also attached the playbook and the proposed SLA addendum for reference. Next calendar step: I’ll send 3 QBR options in a separate calendar message today; please accept one so we can lock the slot.

Thanks again — looking forward to wrapping this up cleanly.
